title: Enterprise-managed settings support any default model - GitHub Changelog
excerpt: You can now set your preferred GitHub Copilot model as the default for new conversations through enterprise-managed settings. This lets you choose the default model that best fits your workflows.…
body_excerpt: Enterprise-managed settings support any default model - GitHub Changelog Skip to content Skip to sidebar / Blog Changelog Docs Customer stories Try GitHub Copilot app Attend GitHub Universe Search Changelog Docs Customer stories Attend GitHub Universe Try GitHub Copilot app Back to changelog Improvement September 2, 2026 • 1 minute read Enterprise-managed settings support any default model You can now set your preferred GitHub Copilot model as the default for new conversations through enterprise-managed settings. This lets you choose the default model that best fits your workflows. You can also customize the default by enterprise team, assigning a different default model based on team membership. Set the model key as overridable and update team configuration files in team-mappings.json so that enterprise teams can choose their own preferred default model. All other users inherit your enterprise default. Model defaults in managed settings are generally available with Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise in the GitHub Copilot app, Copilot CLI, and Visual Studio Code. title: Content exclusions generally available in Copilot app and CLI - GitHub Changelog
excerpt: The GitHub Copilot app and Copilot CLI now respect content exclusion policies configured by enterprise, organization, and repository administrators.
body_excerpt: Content exclusions generally available in Copilot app and CLI - GitHub Changelog Skip to content Skip to sidebar / Blog Changelog Docs Customer stories Try GitHub Copilot app Attend GitHub Universe Search Changelog Docs Customer stories Attend GitHub Universe Try GitHub Copilot app Back to changelog Release September 2, 2026 • 1 minute read Content exclusions generally available in Copilot app and CLI The GitHub Copilot app and Copilot CLI now respect content exclusion policies configured by enterprise, organization, and repository administrators. Copilot won’t use excluded files as context, helping you protect sensitive code across agentic workflows. This is available for Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise customers.
